scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PCs in the IT Department (192.168.1.x) report they cannot reach
their gateway (192.168.1.1) or anything off-subnet. CS Dept PCs
(192.168.2.x) and all other zones are unaffected. Identify the
failure.

injection.action: bring down the bridge that carries IT Dept LAN

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch0 br0 (L2 fabric for IT Dept LAN)
Mechanism: switch0's br0 carries the IT Dept LAN's path to
  router0's 192.168.1.1 SVI. With br0 down, IT hosts lose their
  gateway and all off-subnet reachability. Other subnets are on
  different switches/bridges, so they're unaffected.
Localization: switch0
Root cause: br0 administratively down on switch0
Fix: `ip link set br0 up` on switch0
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br0 up` on switch0

line.command: ip -br link show br0 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The Linux bridge interface `br0` on `switch0` — the virtual switch that interconnects the IT department LAN segment (`lan_it`, 192.168.1.x hosts) with the uplink to `router0` (`link_r0_sw0`).

**Mechanism:** In Kathara, network switches are implemented as Linux bridge devices. `switch0` holds `eth0` (uplink to router0) and `eth1` (downlink to IT-dept hosts) as bridge members. When `br0` is DOWN, the kernel does not forward frames between these two member interfaces, making the bridge a complete black hole. Every IT host becomes L2-isolated from their default gateway (192.168.1.1 on router0's eth0). No ARP replies can cross the switch, so no IP traffic of any kind reaches beyond the segment.

**Localization:** `switch0`, interface `br0`. Both `eth0` and `eth1` are individually UP and LOWER_UP — only the bridge master interface is down. CS department traffic is unaffected because it transits `switch1`, which is fully operational.

**Root cause:** The bridge interface `br0` on `switch0` has been administratively brought down (a `link_down` fault injection), silencing the entire IT department LAN segment from the rest of the network.

**Fix:** On `switch0`, run `ip link set dev br0 up` to restore the bridge to a forwarding state. IT hosts will immediately regain L2 adjacency with router0 and recover off-subnet reachability.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly locates the fault on switch0 (bridge br0) in both the affected component and localization sections.
The agent explicitly identifies the affected switch fabric as br0 on switch0 (the bridge interface).
The agent explicitly states the outage isolates the IT department LAN via switch0/br0 while CS traffic on switch1 remains unaffected, correctly distinguishing scope.
Correct — the proposed remediation exactly matches the expected fix to bring br0 up on switch0 (ip link set dev br0 up), restoring bridge forwarding.

The log shows br0 on switch0 is down while member ports eth0/eth1 are up; startup logs show br0 was commanded up but remains down and there are no kernel/link events or processes implying a flap—supporting an administrative shutdown of the bridge and the provided fix. The investigation and writeup coherently link those observations to L2 isolation of the IT subnet and the recommended remediation.
